current_defects: Deferred and complex-forward shaders use independent fixed vec3(1) light directions and vec3(3) radiance.
The runtime ignores persisted Light components.
The environment is a raw sampler2D equirectangular lookup without cooked irradiance, GGX prefilter, or BRDF LUT.
Production startup parses a source HDR image rather than resolving a cooked environment product.

m5_2Supersession.status: M5.2 GPU light-record declaration added; M5.0 defect hashes remain historical

m5_3Supersession.status: M5.3 shared cluster declarations and diagnostic views added; M5.0/M5.2 hashes remain historical

m5_4Supersession.status: M5.4 authored clustered direct lighting replaces both fixed production lights; all earlier hashes remain historical

m5_5Supersession.status: M5.5 candidate cooked AP1 irradiance, GGX prefilter, F0/F90 split-sum, and radiance cubes replace raw equirectangular production sampling; earlier hashes remain historical

m5_6Supersession.status: M5.6 candidate stabilized directional cascade rendering and shared deferred/forward compare sampling; earlier hashes remain historical

m5_7Supersession.status: M5.7 multi-owner directional visibility plus persistent spot-atlas and tiered point-cube GPU slices supersede only the M5.6 single-owner capacity; M5.6 hashes remain historical

m5_8Supersession.status: M5.8 HDRI Sky plus bounded local reflection-probe GPU assignment, indexed prefiltered cubemaps, boundary blending, and box projection are current; M5.7 hashes remain historical

m5_9Supersession.status: M5.9 bounded spatial PCSS uses physical emitter extent, deterministic raw-depth blocker search, quality ceilings, and fixed-PCF or hard-shadow fallback; M9 owns temporal reconstruction

m5_11Acceptance.status: Accepted 2026-08-13: M5 production light, sky, shadow, reflection-probe, baked-lighting, and qualification-fixture contracts are frozen; later milestones must supersede changed hashes explicitly

m5_13CorrectiveHardening.status: Post-acceptance corrective hardening: local +Z is the common visible emission direction, receiver bias is expressed in world-space shadow texels instead of normalized depth or fixed centimeters, hard/contact edges use compare-then-filter reconstruction, Ultra filtering is denser, high-end directional/spot defaults increase spatial density, and point raw-depth filtering no longer interpolates nonlinear projected depth. Historical acceptance hashes remain unchanged and are explicitly superseded here.

m6_1Supersession.status: M6.1 advances the fixed 832-byte packed-material ABI to schema 3 by replacing its reserved tail with versioned transparency policy fields and moving packed-normal Z reconstruction to a feature bit. M5 acceptance and corrective hashes remain historical; only the three consumers of packed_material.glsl are superseded here, with LegacyTwoBucket captures verified pixel-identical.

m6_2Supersession.status: M6.2 adds classified SortedSurface execution with premultiplied output in a dedicated depth-read-only forward pass. M5 acceptance, corrective, and M6.1 hashes remain historical; only the two complex material programs are superseded here.

m6_3Supersession.status: M6.3 replaces empirical glass camera/thickness constants with the active per-view transport record, exact dielectric Fresnel/TIR, metric ThinGlass paths, and bounded Beer-Lambert absorption. Earlier accepted hashes remain historical; only the two complex material programs are superseded here.

m6_4Supersession.status: M6.4 replaces the repeated single-level compatibility scene copies with one pre-transparency AP1 color pyramid, conservative metric-depth pyramid, projection-aware rough refraction, and probe/sky edge fallback. Earlier accepted hashes remain historical; only the transparent complex-material program is superseded here.

m6_5Supersession.status: M6.5 corrects the current local Alfa headlamp dielectric input and zero-thickness classified-glass composition. Earlier accepted benchmark hashes remain historical; the current sample-car manifest source and transparent complex-material program hashes are superseded here.

m6_6Supersession.status: M6.6 shares the indexed complex-material body with exact and bounded-residual deep-tier local composition. Earlier accepted benchmark hashes remain historical; the current opaque and transparent complex-material programs are superseded here.

m6_7Supersession.status: M6.7 adds the active WeightedOIT accumulation output contract to the shared transparent complex-material body and compile-time excludes the unreachable refraction transport/descriptors from the explicit nonrefractive WeightedOIT shader. Earlier accepted benchmark hashes remain historical; the shared body and ordinary transparent complex-material program are superseded here.

m6_8Supersession.status: M6.8 adds backend-neutral transparency class, fallback, measured interval, selected pyramid mip, retained-layer, and overflow/saturation diagnostics. Deferred opaque/alpha-clip and all shared complex-forward variants expose the same per-view identity without overlapping layered per-draw work identity. Allocation hardening replaces transient local-shadow duplicate-owner storage with deterministic sorted validation while preserving scheduler semantics. Earlier accepted hashes remain historical; only diagnostic shader and allocation-hardening contracts are superseded here.

m7_7Supersession.status: M7.7 caps directional coverage by project/profile policy, retains practical/log splits with world-density diagnostics, reconstructs PCSS filter comparisons bilinearly while retaining raw blocker depth, and makes the Cinematic project tier reachable. Accepted M5/M6 hashes remain historical and are explicitly superseded here.

m7_7BiasSupersession.status: M7.7 adds bounded receiver-plane depth correction and geometric-normal offset in cascade world-texel units, validates the terms with a fixture-owned grazing receiver, and records active bias settings in profiles and captures. Earlier accepted hashes remain historical and are explicitly superseded here.

m7_7CasterVisibilitySupersession.status: M7.7 derives an independent conservative caster set for each refreshed directional cascade, retains unknown bounds fail-visible, and records exact tested/culled caster-cascade telemetry. Earlier accepted hashes remain historical and are explicitly superseded here.

m7_7AffectedBoundsSupersession.status: M7.7 replaces the global directional caster cache key with four backend-owned conservative caster revisions, so entering, leaving, or changing a caster invalidates only affected cascades while the others remain sampleable. Earlier accepted hashes remain historical and are explicitly superseded here.

m7_7GpuSceneShadowSubmissionSupersession.status: M7.7 replaces copied persistent CPU caster packets with compact camera-independent GPU-scene primitive references shared by directional, spot, and point shadows, while retaining explicit direct fallback packets. Vulkan still resolves references to direct indexed draws; device-built shadow indirect commands remain open. Earlier accepted hashes remain historical and are explicitly superseded here.

m7_7DirectionalDeviceCommandSupersession.status: M7.7 builds directional-cascade indexed commands on the device from compact GPU-scene primitive references, reuses one candidate table across cascade output regions, validates fence-delayed device counts against the independent CPU oracle, and retains direct capability, tiny-workload, capacity, invalid-data, mixed-submission, and qualification-reference fallbacks. Earlier accepted hashes remain historical and are explicitly superseded here.

m7_7LocalShadowDeviceCommandSupersession.status: M7.7 extends device-built indexed commands to spot-atlas tiles and point-cube faces. Each refreshed local-light view owns a bounded output region, GPU-scene transform and bindless material identity flow through indirect firstInstance, fence-delayed counts are checked against an independent CPU clip-volume oracle, and direct capability, tiny-workload, capacity, invalid-data, mixed-submission, and qualification-reference fallbacks remain explicit. Earlier accepted hashes remain historical and are explicitly superseded here.

m7_7ShadowCommandOracleGatingSupersessio.status: M7.7 makes per-view CPU shadow visibility an explicit qualification oracle instead of a production device-command dependency. Vulkan retains fence-delayed exact device-count and overflow readback without the oracle, validation builds enable comparison automatically, and --shadow-indirect-qualification-oracle enables it independently. Earlier accepted hashes remain historical and are explicitly superseded here.

m7_7IndependentProbeVisibilitySupersessi.status: M7.7 gives reflection capture an independent compact GpuSceneConsumerProbe submission, mirrors stable primitive owners for self-capture exclusion, performs conservative visibility per scheduled cube face, and retains an explicit direct qualification/fallback path. Earlier accepted hashes remain historical and are explicitly superseded here.

m7_7ProbeGpuSceneCapturePipelineSuperses.status: M7.7 adds a probe-capture graphics pipeline that resolves transform and material identity from the persistent GPU scene for compact casters, preserves the direct packet reference/fallback pipeline, and exposes a probe-only direct qualification switch. Device-built cube-face commands remain a subsequent gate; the paired scene-linear checkpoint is numerically equivalent within one R16 quantization step rather than byte-identical.

m7_7ProbeDeviceCommandSupersession.status: M7.7 gives reflection capture bounded probe-owned candidate, command, and count storage; performs conservative cube-face visibility and stable-owner exclusion in compute; submits compatible bins with indirect-count draws; and retains mixed/direct fallback plus fence-delayed exact count and overflow validation. The accepted nine-primitive fixture produces 33 device commands matching the CPU oracle with zero mismatch or overflow, while the deployable route performs no GPU-owned CPU face tests and retains the preceding capture hash.

m7_7ProbeLodSupersession.status: M7.7 adds independent face-invariant radial LOD selection to reflection-probe device commands. The host admits only resident buffer-compatible LOD prefixes; malformed input retains LOD0; validation compares complete command multisets after the fence; and production repeats neither visibility nor LOD on the CPU. The accepted 2-pixel near/mid/far fixture reduces 7 of 226 commands and 4,508 triangles with zero mismatch/overflow and a byte-identical LOD0 scene capture. LOD0 remains the global default pending reflection-sensitive warmed admission.

m7_7DirectionalShadowLodSupersession.status: M7.7 adds independent density-based LOD selection to directional-cascade device commands. Selection converts cooked object-space error through packed world scale and each cascade's measured world-units-per-texel, the host admits only resident buffer-compatible prefixes, validation compares complete command multisets, and production repeats neither light-view visibility nor shadow LOD on the CPU. The accepted 2-texel dense near/mid/far fixture reduces 21 of 1,243 commands and 13,524 triangles with zero mismatch and a byte-identical LOD0 scene capture. LOD0 remains the global default pending native-4K visual and warmed admission.

m7_7PointShadowLodSupersession.status: M7.7 adds face-invariant radial LOD selection to point-cube device commands. The light position, cube resolution, and conservative bounds produce one LOD shared by all six faces; the host admits only resident buffer-compatible prefixes; validation compares complete command multisets; and production repeats neither point-face visibility nor LOD on the CPU. The accepted 2-texel dense near/mid/far fixture reduces 16 of 565 commands and 11,436 triangles with zero mismatch/overflow and no scene-linear pixel exceeding 1e-6 difference from LOD0. LOD0 remains the global default pending native-4K visual and warmed admission.

m7_7SpotShadowLodSupersession.status: M7.7 adds independent projected-error LOD selection to spot-atlas device commands. The authored spotlight clip transform and atlas-tile resolution drive the conservative perspective bound; the host admits only resident buffer-compatible prefixes; validation compares complete command multisets; and production repeats neither spotlight visibility nor LOD on the CPU. The accepted 2-texel dense near/mid/far fixture reduces 10 of 339 commands and 6,376 triangles with zero mismatch/overflow and a byte-identical LOD0 scene capture. LOD0 remains the global default pending native-4K visual and warmed admission.

m7_7HeterogeneousShadowAdmissionSuperses.status: M7.7 admits production directional, spot, and point device-command submission on a warmed native-4K moving heterogeneous workload. A shadow-only direct-reference switch isolates the comparison from main-view and probe routing. Two reversed-order 600-frame pairs reduce median combined CPU shadow recording by 70.1-70.9%, slightly reduce combined GPU shadow time, and preserve byte-identical final-SDR output. Validation reports exact command-oracle parity and zero mismatch, overflow, fallback, or dropped telemetry counters. Shadow LOD remains default-off pending its separate visual threshold gate.

m7_7ProbeLodWarmedAdmissionSupersession.status: M7.7 completes the reflection-sensitive warmed probe-LOD gate without production admission. A fixture-owned standalone 1024-pixel realtime probe captures all moving high-detail primitives and publishes into visible glossy reflections. Multi-frame capture tickets now finish and publish before newer scene or settings revisions queue a refresh, preserving backend staging lifetime and progress. A 16-pixel bound preserves byte-identical native-4K final-SDR output with exact device/oracle agreement, but removes only 0.9263% of retained capture triangles and produces no repeatable CPU, GPU, wall-time, or memory win. LOD0 remains global and radial probe LOD remains experimental.

m7_7ShadowLodWarmedAdmissionSupersession.status: M7.7 completes the conventional shadow-LOD visual and warmed admission gate without changing the global default. Native-4K directional, spot, and point threshold sweeps remain visually bounded through eight shadow texels; the warmed moving dense-geometry fixture reports exact device/oracle command agreement and zero overflow. Eight texels remove 1.2685% of combined shadow triangles and save 0.007-0.011 ms of combined shadow GPU time, but CPU shadow recording regresses and reversed-order whole-frame results do not repeat. LOD0 remains the production default and shadow LOD remains an explicit experiment.

m7_7ShadowMembershipCacheSupersession.status: M7.7 publishes camera-independent shadow and probe consumer membership with stable revisions, removing per-frame application scans. Vulkan directional, spot, and point shadow submission caches geometry/material bins and candidate layouts across transform-only frames while continuing per-light device visibility and LOD compaction. Membership revisions invalidate for scene epochs, enablement, consumer masks, LOD ceilings, material/bin state, and geometry products. LOD policy changes and shadow-buffer reallocations also invalidate the backend cache.

m7_7OpaqueShadowPositionFetchSupersessio.status: M7.7 specializes opaque conventional-shadow vertex fetch without duplicating geometry storage. Direct and GPU-scene directional, spot, and point pipelines use position-only shaders and one Vulkan vertex attribute; alpha-masked casters retain position, vertex color, UV0, and UV1. Two reversed-order native-4K pairs save 0.082-0.088 ms of combined shadow raster time with byte-identical final-SDR output. A separate compact position buffer remains rejected pending a memory-inclusive benefit.

m7_7ShadowQualityClosureSupersession.status: M7.7 closes the conventional-shadow quality matrix with a deterministic near-to-far camera sweep over thin, alpha-clipped, double-sided, close-contact, and grazing-angle geometry. Validation reports exact device/oracle command agreement with zero mismatched bins, overflow, or direct fallback. Native-4K direct and device-generated captures are byte-identical at both sweep extremes, while visual inspection confirms stable finite contact shadows and a fully clipped alpha caster with no residual shadow.

m7_8VirtualShadowResidencyContractSupers.status: M7.8 defines the backend-neutral sparse virtual-shadow residency contract and deterministic CPU reference planner, maps its bounded dimensions to a default-off Vulkan allocation, and freezes directional receiver marking plus bounded compaction. ABI v2 uses signed world-page coordinates and snapped clip origins so camera scrolling preserves cache identity. Raw marking and the deterministic reference compactor have Debug/Release RTX 4090 parity. The first global-bitonic candidate was rejected near 845 ms; its hierarchical replacement retains exact 4,096-receiver and 65,536-mark parity and measures 0.145792/0.145984 ms Debug/Release median with device-local storage. Two frame-owned aligned device-local working sets now persist the admitted compute layout; immutable per-frame descriptors and the shared direct mark/compact chain now pass exact populated/empty reuse under synchronization validation at 0.148512/0.147264 ms Debug/Release for 65,536 receivers. The sampled-D32 region producer now reconstructs every pixel and chains exact requests through forward/reverse depth, odd offset regions, invalid values and perspective/singular cameras; its 4,095-pixel chain measures 0.067904/0.067872 ms Debug/Release. Full-view depth accumulation now uses bounded per-clip page cells without spatial subsampling or extra tracked buffer/image storage. Exact odd two-clip and native-4K requests and overflow telemetry match under synchronization validation; the full4K chain measures 0.569824/0.569504 ms Debug/Release. Camera-driven clip construction now preserves signed world pages across snapped positive/negative scroll and retains fixed light-space depth; generated CPU/GPU guard fallback agrees exactly. The four-level builder measures 0.186163 us Release with fixed-capacity storage. Live CPU publication now derives the first selected light's packet from actual camera and caster spheres even on conventional cache-hit frames. A monotonic publisher conservatively retains/expands quantized depth limits and suppresses unknown-bound packets; all 12 validation smoke frames publish four levels at revision 1. Both caster layers use the complete content revision conservatively. Per-slot immutable packet snapshots now upload 1536 checked packed clip bytes through an optional graph pass. Non-owning imported-buffer bindings enforce retired/distinct slots and persistent write hazards; a 12-frame validation launch uploads both slots without added GPU storage. Live opaque scene depth now drives full-view accumulation and compaction through ordered graph passes; both retired slots validate request metadata. An explicit full-depth CPU oracle matches native-4K moving-camera request addresses and coverage exactly. Matched captures remain byte-identical, and five paired runs record demand-only overhead rather than production admission. Request readbacks add 262208 qualification bytes; full-depth readbacks are separately opt-in. Whole-frame virtual-path admission, residency updates, page raster and sampling remain open; conventional shadows remain active. A shared RHI physical-tile layout and pending-page crop now define rasterized borders, interior UVs, conservative sphere eligibility and strict owner/projection/requested-layer revision rejection; scroll preserves the cropped world volume. The Vulkan resource owner consumes the same checked layout without allocation growth. This is a raster-projection prerequisite, not GPU residency or page drawing. Residency ABI v1 now defines lossless 48-byte keys and 96-byte resident records with full UUID, signed 64-bit pages, revisions, frame age, physical slot and independent layer validity. A checked compact-request bridge is used by retired-slot validation and compares full identity/revisions against the live CPU oracle. A bounded serial qualification shader now consumes full-key requests and resident records in a private hardware test; 14 oracle dispatches and five atomic rejection checks pass. The 256-request/256-slot/64-update GPU median is 10.5083/10.8429 ms Debug/Release, so this reference is explicitly rejected for live production integration. It validates identity, priority/coverage/full-address ordering, separate layer invalidation, eviction, budget overflow and fallback, but does not raster or commit pages. Live runtime GPU storage and marking ABI v2 remain unchanged; a scalable allocator, raster, generation-safe completion and shared sampling remain open.
